title: The Educated Barbarian: Meditations analysis (part. 21)
summary: Commentary on Meditations passages about the social spirit, mastering bodily impulses, living each day as an addition, and reacting to adversity. He uses a fresh abusive copyright strike on his channel as an example and ties practice-without-affectation to training on schedule, not motivation.
claims: Individualism isn't selfishness: you build yourself up to be useful to the group, since a group of strong individuals is far more powerful than many weak ones
Societies that sacrifice individuality for collectivity create weak collectives where weakness becomes a value (slave morality)
What separates humans from animals is mastering base instincts; you must acknowledge your shadow and impulses, then control them rather than deny them
Live as if in a dream (Musashi, Hagakure): detached and free of anxiety, treating each new day as an extra addition to seize
A strong adverse reaction makes an event worse: it wastes energy and teaches your brain that small things are big deals, training you to be a wimp
Treat setbacks as opportunities to learn rather than slights
His channel just got an abusive copyright strike (1 of 3); his lesson was that copyright law is blurry and he must be more careful, since the world is impersonal forces
Development of the mind cannot be separated from development of the body; both require practice
You can't only train or study when motivated; betterment must be scheduled and unavoidable, which is why accountability matters in lifting
Life is like wrestling rather than solo dancing: you are surrounded by forces and must keep your guard up
